# Linux syscall coverage: Osum vs the FreeBSD Linuxulator (measured 20.11.2026)

Sources
* Osum: `tools/unterbau/t_sysall.c` probes every x86-64 syscall number 0-459 (table generated by `tools/unterbau/gen_sysall_table.py` from FreeBSD `sys/amd64/linux/syscalls.master`) in a forked child; ENOSYS = GAP. Skipped (not probed): exit, exit_group, rt_sigreturn, clone, vfork, reboot, clone3 (clone3 taken from `t_sysgap2`: GAP) and the unassigned range 335-423. Measured on main 9d4a7ce95, QEMU KVM: 308 PASS, 56 GAP of 364 probed (+ clone3 = 57).
* FreeBSD: `sys/amd64/linux/syscalls.master` (365 entries: 310 STD, 40 NOPROTO, 15 UNIMPL) and `sys/compat/linux/linux_dummy.c` (62 `DUMMY()` stubs, each returns ENOSYS, see `linux_util.h`), main branch, fetched 20.11.2026.
* "PASS" only means "not ENOSYS": a stub that answers EPERM/EINVAL (e.g. `unshare`, `setns`, `perf_event_open`) counts as PASS here. Real semantics are checked by the other `t_*` tests.

## Numbers

| | Osum | FreeBSD Linuxulator |
|---|---|---|
| answers (not ENOSYS) with real code | 308 of 364 probed | 310 STD + 40 NOPROTO entries, minus 62 DUMMY stubs |
| missing / ENOSYS | 57 | 62 DUMMY + 15 UNIMPL |
| in common: both implemented | 271 | |
| Osum implemented, FreeBSD only a stub (ENOSYS) | 34 | |
| Osum missing, FreeBSD implemented | 11 (`creat`, `ustat`, `sysfs`, `modify_ldt`, `_sysctl`, `quotactl`, `open_by_handle_at`, `kexec_file_load`, `rseq`, `clone3`, `map_shadow_stack`) | |
| both missing | 46 (28 FreeBSD stubs + 18 numbers FreeBSD does not list) | |

Osum is ahead of FreeBSD where it counts for apps: `vhangup`, `pivot_root`, `adjtimex`, `swapoff`, `mbind`, `set_mempolicy`, `get_mempolicy`, `add_key`, `request_key`, `keyctl`, `unshare`, `tee`, `vmsplice`, `signalfd4`, `perf_event_open`, `fanotify_init`, `fanotify_mark`, `clock_adjtime`, `setns`, `process_vm_readv`, `process_vm_writev`, `sched_setattr`, `execveat`, `mlock2`, `preadv2`, `pwritev2`, `io_pgetevents`, `pidfd_send_signal`, `pidfd_open`, `openat2`, `pidfd_getfd`, `process_madvise`, `cachestat`, `fchmodat2`.

## Osum GAPs by priority

P1 = blocks or badly degrades a target program class, P2 = program falls back but loses features/speed, P3 = rare / obsolete / never for apps. Obsolete never-used numbers (`uselib`, `create_module`, `get_kernel_syms`, `query_module`, `nfsservctl`, `getpmsg`, `putpmsg`, `afs_syscall`, `tuxcall`, `security`, `epoll_ctl_old`, `epoll_wait_old`, `vserver`) and the new numbers 457-459 are left out (FreeBSD does not implement them either).

| prio | nr | syscall | FreeBSD linuxulator | who needs it / evidence | effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 154 | `modify_ldt` | implemented | Wine WoW64 (32-bit Windows apps): 32-bit TEB/FS segment setup (signal_x86_64.c modify_ldt); not needed for 64-bit PE | L |

Evidence level: Wine rows come from the Wine source (see docs/WINE-FEASIBILITY.md) and a Linux `strace -f` of `wine cmd /c echo`; the other "who needs it" entries are knowledge-based estimates (not measured on Osum).

## What the syscall list does NOT show (more important than any row above)

* Address space: Osum user memory lives in fixed windows (user data 0x40000000-0x52C00000, lazy window 0x80000000-0x1000000000); `MAP_FIXED` works only inside them and never for file-backed `MAP_SHARED` (`kernel/sys/sysmem.fi`). Wine needs fixed mappings at 0x10000-0x110000, 0x7f000000-0x7fff0000, 0x7ffe0000 (user_shared_data) and 0x7ffffe000000-0x7fffffff0000: all fail (guest log, 20.11.2026).
* Kernel mechanisms, not syscalls: 32-bit compat mode for WoW64, `/dev/ntsync`, DRM/GPU.
